solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spades have to be put in soil

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A gardener is told the spades must be buried in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spades' pulls towards digging, but here it is only the suit letter, and 'have' is the verb own.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: seed is sown by being placed in the ground.

clue.text: Spotted story about getting shot outside

parts.note: a shy is a throw or attempt, as at a coconut shy
the plot of a story
c = circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone was spotted reading a story about a shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a fairground stall where you throw at coconuts, so a shy is a shot or throw. PLOT and C sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: marked with spots or blotches.

clue.text: Initially, it looks like this

parts.note: reads as 'at first'; it means the answer is built from initial letters
reads as a casual remark; it is the promise of a screen showing exactly what will print

explanation.surface: A remark that something looks, from the start, just like this.
explanation.walkthrough: WYSIWYG is the computing term for an editor whose screen shows exactly what will print: What You See Is What You Get, reduced to its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The acronym's whole meaning is that the thing looks like what you see, so the clue paraphrases the phrase it abbreviates.

clue.text: Set of dance moves without expression

indicators.note: letters that move shift position, so 'set of dance' changes order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A deadpan dancer performs a routine with no expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set of dance moves' reads as one phrase, a routine; the break comes after 'dance', making 'moves' the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a face as unmoving as stone shows no feeling.

clue.text: Leaves squad short

indicators.note: something short falls short of its full length, so the squad loses its last letter

parts.note: TEAM minus its final M

explanation.surface: A squad heads off while short of players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, someone departing; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by material: the drink is brewed from dried leaves, and loose tea is sold as tea leaves.

clue.text: I depend on no shelter, up to a point

parts.note: the word itself
a tent is a shelter
the word itself
to depend on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A camper insists they need no shelter, though only up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts I RELY below NO TENT, reversing the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for partial agreement: true up to a point is true only in part.

clue.text: I could "self-slur" circulating this?

indicators.note: letters that circulate go round and come back in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

explanation.surface: Someone muses that telling everything might mean slurring themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads straight too: putting damaging facts about yourself into circulation is a self-slur.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: making everything known, the discreditable parts included, is exactly circulating a slur on yourself.

clue.text: Transported box with handles

parts.note: reads as a crate being carried; it is a set mounted in a moving vehicle, such as a lorry
reads as carrying grips; handles are the nicknames its users go by on air

explanation.surface: A box with carrying handles is moved.
explanation.walkthrough: CB (citizens' band) radio is the short-range set used by truckers, who call themselves by nicknames known as handles.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun on handles: a vehicle radio whose operators are known by call-names.

clue.text: City, within a week or so, deteriorates

parts.note: a week is a matter of days
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A city falls into ruin within about a week.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rot or wear away is to grow worse.

clue.text: Sweet little memory about old departed

parts.note: a whit is a very little amount
an echo of the past is a memory of it
c = circa, about
O is the abbreviation for old
the late means the dead, the departed

explanation.surface: A fond little memory of someone who has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet little memory' reads as one phrase; 'Sweet' is split off as the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: in British English a sweet is any confection, chocolate included.

clue.text: See group with judge in despair

parts.note: lo! = see! look!
a set is a group
a judge hears a case

explanation.surface: Someone watches a group with a judge and falls into despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' is a verb here, to hear a case.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: heart stands for courage, and losing your courage and hope is despairing.

clue.text: Shed tears over one line about musical content

indicators.note: turning about faces the other way, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: to cry is to shed tears
I is the Roman numeral one; it goes inside CRY, giving CIRY
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone weeps over a single line in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: CIRY plus L is CIRYL, which turned about gives the answer. The surface's tears over a line are the mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the words of a song are what it contains besides its tune.

clue.text: Viz advice for caravan owner

definitions.meaning: viz. is short for Latin videlicet, namely
a caravan is a trailer home pulled behind a car, so the advice is to pull it

explanation.surface: A tip for someone who owns a caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'tow it', the answer is what you tell a caravan owner; read as one phrase it is the old legal 'namely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Viz. and to wit both introduce a specification, meaning 'namely'; the second sense is the same letters split as TOW IT.

clue.text: Brand of drink — pop, yellow bottles

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside

parts.note: canary yellow
pop is father, dad

explanation.surface: An ad line for a yellow fizzy pop sold in bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'Brand of drink' ahead of it, 'pop' reads as fizzy drink; it is father, and 'bottles' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a real brand of ginger ale and mixers.

clue.text: Groom gets nothing in it in an arranged marriage

indicators.note: nothing is put in it, so O goes inside IT
an arranged set is put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to groom hair is to comb it
O (nothing) inside IT gives IOT; with IN AN these letters are arranged

explanation.surface: A bridegroom brings nothing to an arranged marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' and 'marriage' make a wedding; the groom is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: a marriage of flavours or ideas is a joining of them.

clue.text: Tall order for embassy

parts.note: tall = high
a commission is an order for work

explanation.surface: An embassy is making an unreasonable demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tall order' is a set phrase for a hard demand; split it into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: Commonwealth countries call their embassies in one another high commissions.

clue.text: Watch broadcast on wild orgy

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters of ORGY scatter

parts.note: a message broadcast has been sent out
the letters of ORGY rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone watches a wild orgy on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like viewing; it is guard duty.
explanation.definitionFit: An old military term: a soldier's turn of guard duty, a watch.

clue.text: She has been fairly treated

parts.note: reads as any woman's story; she is a type of woman
reads as handled justly; it means treated so as to be fair-haired

explanation.surface: A woman has been dealt with justly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairly treated' reads as justly handled; it means her hair was treated to make it fair, with peroxide bleach.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun on fair: someone whose hair is bleached light has been treated to become fair.

clue.text: Letter I left in printer?

parts.note: Epson is a printer maker; the ? flags an example
the word itself
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A letter I left in the printer tray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like a sheet of mail, fitting the printer; it is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Catching nothing snooping around

parts.note: nosing around is snooping
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A snoop comes away having caught nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snooping around' reads as a phrase, but 'around' is the instruction to wrap the snooping round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by method: to snare an animal in a running loop of rope is to catch it.

clue.text: Winter mist, poor forecasting — rants about leaves

indicators.note: a poor forecast is a bad one, so FORECASTING is jumbled
the rants are scattered about the word rather than together
the rants leave, so their letters are taken out

parts.note: the whole word to start from
R, A, N, T, S are removed, leaving F O E C I G to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster botched a mist warning, and someone rants about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RANTS are all inside FORECASTING, though scattered, which is what 'about' allows.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: fog made of suspended ice crystals, found in very cold winters.

clue.text: Bird caught while very alert

parts.note: c = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation
as = while, at the same time as
so = very
wary = alert to danger

explanation.surface: A bird was trapped despite being on its guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a nature story of a bird snared despite its caution; 'caught' is really the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a large flightless bird of New Guinea and northern Australia.

clue.text: Do that which makes quiet impossible?

definitions.text: Do that which makes quiet impossible?

parts.note: sh! is a call for quiet
out = out of the question, impossible

explanation.surface: A riddle: what act rules out any quiet?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, while 'quiet impossible' also spells the letters in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: raising your voice loudly is the act that makes quiet impossible.

clue.text: Knock down a bloke

parts.note: to fell is to knock down
the word itself

explanation.surface: An order to knock a man to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloke is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial synonym: both are casual words for a man.

clue.text: Apparently it is a downtown area

definitions.text: Apparently it is a downtown area

parts.note: reads as a vague 'it seems'; it points at the letters IT, which sit in the middle of CITY
the straight sense: the central part of a town

explanation.surface: A remark that some place seems to be downtown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' flags the joke: IT really is the inner part of CITY, since those two letters sit in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain sense plus a pun: the inner city is the central district of a city, and IT is inside C-IT-Y.

clue.text: Egg noodle

definitions.meaning: the egg of a louse, found in hair
noodle is old slang for a fool or simpleton

explanation.surface: An egg noodle, as in a noodle dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg noodles are a food, so the two words look like one thing; split them. The fool sense is short for nitwit.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a louse egg, and a fool, short for nitwit.

clue.text: Out to lunch after Fred's partner snaps

parts.note: Ginger Rogers danced with Fred Astaire
out to lunch = crazy, nuts

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper and snaps, as though out to lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snaps' looks like a verb, losing your temper; it is the noun, the biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: the ginger biscuits Americans call gingersnaps are ginger nuts in Britain.

clue.text: Language introduced by Ludwig Boltzmann

indicators.note: the language is brought in by, carried inside, the physicist's name

parts.note: ludwIG BOltzmann

explanation.surface: A new language brought in by the physicist Ludwig Boltzmann.
explanation.walkthrough: Boltzmann was an Austrian physicist, which sends a solver towards German; the language is Nigerian.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a major language of south-eastern Nigeria.
